A.explanation: This value is 1000 times too small, from failing to convert $250 \text{ mm}^2$ and $0.10 \text{ mm}$ correctly to metres.

B.explanation: Using $F = 2500 \text{ N}$ per rod in $E = FL/Ax$ gives $2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N m}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: This uses the full $10 \text{ kN}$ for one rod instead of dividing equally between the four rods.

D.explanation: This uses the full $10 \text{ kN}$ for one rod and also has a power-of-ten error from the $\text{mm}$ to $\text{m}$ conversions.

hints: Notice the $10 \text{ kN}$ weight is equally shared, so find the compressive force $F$ in one rod of length $2.0 \text{ m}$.
Recall $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = FL/Ax$ and convert $250 \text{ mm}^2$ to $2.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$ and $0.10 \text{ mm}$ to $1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.
Calculate stress $F/A$ for one rod and strain $x/L$, then divide to get $E$ in $\text{N m}^{-2}$ and check the power of ten.
walkthrough: The four rods equally support $10 \text{ kN}$, so the force on one rod is $F = 10000/4 = 2500 \text{ N}$ in compression.
Young modulus is $E = \text{stress}/\text{strain} = (F/A)/(x/L) = FL/Ax$, which applies to compression as well as extension.
Convert to SI units: $A = 250 \text{ mm}^2 = 250 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2 = 2.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$ and $x = 0.10 \text{ mm} = 1.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$ with $L = 2.0 \text{ m}$.
Stress in one rod is $F/A = 2500/(2.5 \times 10^{-4}) = 1.0 \times 10^{7} \text{ N m}^{-2}$ and strain is $x/L = (1.0 \times 10^{-4})/2.0 = 5.0 \times 10^{-5}$.
Hence $E = (1.0 \times 10^{7})/(5.0 \times 10^{-5}) = 2.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ N m}^{-2}$. This is option B.
